claims.text: The artifacts describe one trip, so the rider's limb (a) burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: EV-TRIP-00526, EV-GPS-00526 and EV-FARE-00526 each carry trip_id TRP-00526, and the trace window (first fix 2026-09-14T23:36:40, last fix 2026-09-15T00:04:40) matches the trip record's started_at and ended_at. There is no identifier mismatch and no POL-RD-10(2) escalation trigger on identity.

The rider is not a serial deviation claimant, so no extra corroboration burden attaches to this claim: EV-RPROF-00526 records deviation_claims_60d 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0, far below the four-claims-and-one-substantiated threshold in POL-RD-08, so the additional-corroboration condition that clause imposes on a sub-30% excess is not engaged against this rider.

No rider-instruction exoneration is open to the driver under POL-RD-04: the chat log for this trip, EV-CHAT-00526, carries message_count 0 and an empty messages array, so there is no rider message, no timestamp and no waypoint_hint, and the corroboration test POL-RD-04 requires (vehicle passing within 200 m of a chat-resolved waypoint, or travelling a named road) cannot be run at all, let alone in the driver's favour.

No road-closure exoneration is available under POL-RD-03 either, and I disclose the impairment of the artifact I cite for that absence: the only traffic-advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00526-01, is MISSING - it has no payload and carries weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - so it names no road or segment, sets no validity window, and supplies no shortest_lawful_alternative_km. Per POL-GEN-02 a MISSING artifact can carry no fact and its absence is itself citable, so the driver's 'the meter is the fare' points to no advisory and no clause.

The driver has no alternative baseline to measure against on this record: EV-TRIP-00526 shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so the POL-RD-05 relocation route cannot be run, and it shows vehicle_type RYDE_TAXI with solo_optimal_distance_km null, so the POL-RD-12 pooled-itinerary carve-out does not apply. The booked 15.6 km optimal is the only baseline in evidence.

I do not put the rider's case on a distance deviation, because the trace that governs under POL-RD-01 cannot carry one: derived.deviation reports excess_km 0.17 against an optimal of 15.6 km, that is 1.09%, below both the 20% and the 0.8 km establishment gates, and the governing trace_distance_km 15.77 displaces the rounded actual_distance_km 15.8. On the distance arithmetic the rider cannot pass the threshold and I concede it.

The rider's grievance is not the corridor but the price mode, and the record cannot resolve it. EV-TRIP-00526's optimal_route_source records that the rider selected RYDE_X on a display of 'up to 26.00' and that the platform dispatched RYDE_TAXI, while EV-FARE-00526 bills the trip on the METERED taxi card with quoted_fare_sgd null and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. POL-RD-02 runs only on a deviation established under POL-RD-01, and POL-RD-11 runs only on fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted_fare_sgd (signed POL-GEN-03 under which ESCALATE holds the amount rather than collecting it); no clause in this policy can price the trip the rider says was sold, and the display figure survives only as free text in a field the POL-RD-05 notes say must not be read as a governing figure. The ruling therefore cannot be made at the platform's 0.70 confidence floor, and POL-RD-10(1) requires escalation, which holds the disputed 24.29 rather than collecting it.

claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace — which POL-RD-01 makes the governing measurement over the rounded trip_record copy — records 15.77 km between the pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 15.6 km. That is an excess of 0.17 km and 1.09%, and the derived deviation status on the artifact reads expressly 'no deviation'. Both POL-RD-01 gates must pass and neither does: the excess is far below the 0.8 km absolute gate and far below the 20% proportional gate. Even on the non-governing trip_record figure of 15.8 km the excess is 0.2 km, still under both gates. No deviation exists, so under POL-RD-01 the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The trace is complete and unimpaired, so it is the best evidence in the bundle and no softer reconstruction is available to the rider: 169 fixes at a 10 second cadence against an expected interval of 10 seconds, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, with the admissibility pre-pass returning COMPLETE at weight 1.0. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so there is no impaired stretch, no straight-line measurement rule, and no requirement to corroborate the trace from an independent source.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence, that the artifacts describe this trip and that an excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The identifying facts are not in dispute — trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00526 — but limb (b) fails: the unimpaired trace yields 0.17 km and 1.09%, below both gates. The burden never shifts to the driver, the claim is not sustained on POL-RD-01 evidence for this trip, and the present payment state stands.

This trip was dispatched and billed as RYDE_TAXI and the fare_breakdown's fare_model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE. The POL-RD-11 upfront-quote route is therefore closed, and the only distance-and-time recomputation the policy offers — POL-RD-02 — runs solely where a deviation is first established under POL-RD-01, which it is not. On top of that, the ledger's charged_total is SGD 24.29 (base 3.80 + distance 11.85 + time 7.84 + platform fee 0.80), which is below the SGD 26.00 ceiling the rider says they selected, so even taken entirely on the rider's own account no overcharge is shown.

There is no billing-integrity defect for POL-RD-09 to correct. The fare_breakdown carries no ERP gantry charges at all (erp_lines total 0.00, tolls_erp 0.00, erp_gantries empty), no airport surcharge — consistent with a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport — no waiting-time fee and no promo discount. Every charged line has a counterpart in the trip record, the component lines sum exactly to charged_total, and no phantom line is refundable under POL-RD-09(4) and no pass-through correction is due.

Any repeat-deviation uplift is unavailable on the clause's own field tests. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so POL-RD-06 establishes no pattern: the flag count is nowhere near 3, and the ratio (0.00) is nowhere near the 0.05 required with at least 40 completed trips. No FULL_REFUND uplift under limb (b) and no driver-conduct referral under limb (c) is available on this record, and the materiality condition that would even require the check is not met.

The driver asserts no exoneration under POL-RD-03, because the record contains no traffic advisory for the optimal corridor: EV-ADVIS-00526-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, and is weighted 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — the absence itself is citable, and the driver does not present it as if it were evidence. None is needed in any event: with the trace showing the vehicle never left the optimal corridor by more than 0.17 km, there is no excess for any exculpatory clause to excuse.

The ruling the driver seeks is NO_ACTION, and under POL-GEN-03 that is a driver-favourable outcome here rather than a null one. NO_ACTION is party-relative: this is a rider-filed dispute and the ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so leaving the present state undisturbed leaves the fare with the driver and restores nothing to the rider. No trigger for terminal escalation under POL-RD-10 exists — the trace is complete at weight 1.0, the trip identifiers all match, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact, and the arithmetic refund is nil — so the case can and should be decided, not held.

ruling.explanation: To the rider and the driver: the fare on trip TRP-00526 stays as charged, and here is why. THE ROUTE. POL-RD-01 decides a route deviation on the GPS trace, and the governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 15.77 km — not the rounded trip_record copy of 15.8 km, which the clause forbids citing for the threshold test. Against the booked optimal of 15.6 km the excess is 0.17 km, or 1.09%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be BOTH over 0.8 km absolute AND over 20% of optimal; it fails both gates, and the artifact's own derived deviation status reads 'no deviation'. No deviation is established, so the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised, and POL-RD-02's fare recomputation does not run (the ledger's illustrative recomputed_fare of 22.46 and refund of 1.85 are not applied). The trace is unimpaired: 169 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s — schema status COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and policy-clean under POL-RD-07(a)-(c). THE PRICE-MODE COMPLAINT. The record shows the rider selected RYDE_X on a display of 'up to 26.00' and the platform dispatched RYDE_TAXI; that is the rider's real grievance. On the money, the fare_breakdown is fare_model METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 (upfront quotes) does not apply, and POL-RD-02 runs only on an established deviation, which this is not. The charged total is SGD 24.29 — base 3.80 + distance 11.85 + time 7.84 + platform fee 0.80 — which is below the 26.00 ceiling the rider says was displayed, so no overcharge against that ceiling is shown. The rider's stated figure of 46.50 is supported by no artifact; the ledger at weight 1.0 shows 24.29. No clause in the ROUTE_DEVIATION policy prices a 'wrong product dispatched' complaint; that open question is noted here rather than turned into a referral, because no clause produces one. NO BILLING-INTEGRITY DEFECT. There are no ERP gantry charges (erp_lines total 0.00), no airport surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo discount, and the component lines sum exactly to the charged total, so no POL-RD-09(4) correction and no billing-integrity referral arise. ESCALATION. The rider asks for ESCALATE under POL-RD-10(1). I decline: POL-RD-10 is a closed list and none of its triggers fire. The trace is unimpaired and all three instruments carry TRP-00526, so (2) and (3) do not apply; the timestamps agree, so (4) does not apply; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or field-lacking artifact — the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00526-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and its absence is citable, but no one relies on it and no closure is asserted — so (5) does not apply; no POL-RD-02 refund is computed, so (6) does not apply; the sides are not in mutually contradictory admissible evidence of comparable strength, because the trip record's note of the product switch is contradicted by nothing, so (7) does not apply; and every charge line has a counterpart, so (8) does not apply. The deciding fact — that no deviation exists — is carried by the GPS trace and the trip record, both at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and the ruling is not below the 0.70 floor. NO REPEAT-DEVIATION REFERRAL. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days, far below the 3-flag or 0.05-ratio test in POL-RD-06, so there is no pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The present state stands: charged 24.29, refund_issued 0.00, payment_status CHARGED. No money moves and there are no referrals.

Rider and driver: the record decides this case on a measurement neither side disputes. The GPS trace, EV-GPS-00526, measures the journey at 15.77 km; the trip record's booked optimal, EV-TRIP-00526, is 15.6 km. The excess is 0.17 km, or 1.09%. POL-RD-01 will find a deviation only if the excess is BOTH more than 0.8 km AND more than 20% of the optimal; it is neither, so no route deviation exists and the fare stands on the distance-and-time lines. The trace is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes — 169 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 s, admissibility weight 1.0 — so POL-RD-07's gap rules never engage and no independent corroboration is required.

The fare, EV-FARE-00526, is METERED: charged_total SGD 24.29, made up of base fare 3.80 + distance 11.85 + time 7.84 + platform fee 0.80, with no ERP or toll lines, no airport surcharge (the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), no waiting-time fee and no promo discount, and every charged line has a counterpart in the trip record. POL-RD-02 recomputes the fare only where a deviation is first established under POL-RD-01, and none is; POL-RD-11 applies only to an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with a non-null quoted_fare_sgd, and this trip is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null. Neither pricing clause can run, and there is no billing-integrity line for POL-RD-09(4) to correct.

Rider: your grievance is that you selected RYDE_X on a display reading 'up to 26.00' and the platform dispatched a metered taxi. That is recorded on EV-TRIP-00526 (optimal_route_source). But the amount actually charged is SGD 24.29 — below the SGD 26.00 ceiling you say you chose — and the ledger shows no higher charge. On your own account you were not charged more than the maximum you selected, and the route-deviation policy contains no clause that refunds a fare because the product mode changed. Your advocate's request to escalate under POL-RD-10(1) is declined: that trigger asks whether my confidence falls below the platform floor of 0.70, and it does not. The facts that decide this case are carried by EV-GPS-00526, EV-TRIP-00526 and EV-FARE-00526, each at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. A clause whose conditions are simply not met (POL-RD-11) is inapplicable, not undecidable, and that does not make the record too thin to rule on.

Driver: your NO_ACTION position is granted — on a rider-filed dispute it leaves the SGD 24.29 charge in place. No repeat-deviation pattern exists (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days), so there is no POL-RD-06 FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. The only impaired artifact, the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00526-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no fact; its absence is noted but decides nothing, because no road-closure exoneration was asserted by either side. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10(2)–(8) is present.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The charged fare of SGD 24.29 stands; no refund is due and no driver compensation is payable. Confidence 0.90.

To the rider and the driver: I begin with the route, because that is what this category decides. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00526) is complete and unimpaired — 169 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, empty gaps, zero-second maximum inter-fix gap — and, as POL-RD-01 requires, its trace_distance_km of 15.77 km governs over the rounded 15.8 km copy on the trip record. Against the booked optimal of 15.6 km on EV-TRIP-00526 that is an excess of 0.17 km, or 1.09%. POL-RD-01 puts two gates in the way and both must pass: an excess greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% of optimal. Neither is met, so no route deviation is established and the rider's distance case fails. That is decisive under POL-RD-01 — 'no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip' — and it follows that the burden under POL-RD-08 stops at the rider's limb (b). Because no deviation is established, the POL-RD-02 recomputation never runs. I note for transparency that the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00526) carries a conditional 1.85 recomputed-fare difference between the charged 24.29 and a recomputed 22.46; that figure exists only if a deviation is first established, and it is not, so it cannot be paid out. POL-RD-11 is likewise closed: the fare model on EV-FARE-00526 is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, not UPFRONT_QUOTE. No billing-integrity defect exists for POL-RD-09(4) to correct — there are no ERP or toll lines (0.00), no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee and no promo, and the lines (base 3.80 + distance 11.85 + time 7.84 + platform fee 0.80) sum exactly to the charged 24.29 — and the driver was not under-billed on distance (15.8 km billed against 15.77 km traced), so no POL-RD-04 compensation arises. On the rider's 'up to 26' point I have read the record and do not dismiss it lightly: EV-TRIP-00526's optimal_route_source records that the rider selected RYDE_X on a display of 'up to 26.00' and that the platform dispatched RYDE_TAXI, and the driver's own statement confirms he is a metered taxi. But no clause in this policy prices a product- or fare-mode switch. POL-RD-02 runs only on a deviation established under POL-RD-01 (not established); POL-RD-11 runs only on fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted_fare_sgd (this trip is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null); POL-RD-09(4) is confined to a gantry the trace never crosses or an airport surcharge on a non-airport-origin trip; and the 'up to 26.00' figure survives only as free text in a field whose contents the policy says must not be read as a governing figure. I also note that the charged total, 24.29, sits below the 26.00 ceiling the rider says they chose, so on the rider's own figures no overcharge is shown. Whether the platform should have honoured the RYDE_X selection is a real open question, and it belongs here in this explanation rather than in a referral or an escalation; the rider may raise the product switch through the appropriate channel. The rider advocate's request that I hold the case is declined. Escalation is not warranted: the trace is complete and unimpaired, so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged; EV-TRIP-00526, EV-GPS-00526 and EV-FARE-00526 all read TRP-00526 and their timestamps agree, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) are not engaged; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact — the absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00526-01 carries weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, can carry no fact, and nothing was decided on it — so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged; no charge line is unmatched, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged; and my confidence is above the 0.70 floor. Finally the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check finds no pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250), so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral, and in any event no material deviation required the check. Outcome: NO_ACTION. This is party-relative — on this rider-filed dispute it leaves the 24.29 charge in place and refunds nothing; the ledger's payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stand. The figures I used are charged_total 24.29, optimal_distance_km 15.6, trace_distance_km 15.77, excess 0.17 km / 1.09%.
